items.question: What is an MDMA?
items.answer: MDMA refers to Medical Device Marketing Authorization. The applicable route and documentation depend on the device and its regulatory context.

items.question: Do foreign manufacturers need local representation?
items.answer: Local representation requirements and responsibilities need to be assessed for the manufacturer and selected pathway. We can help clarify the practical coordination required.

items.question: Can existing FDA, Health Canada or CE documentation be used?
items.answer: Existing evidence can inform the assessment, but it should be reviewed against the Saudi pathway and current product documentation before assumptions are made.

items.question: When should we start?
items.answer: Start before a commercial launch date is fixed. An early readiness review helps surface documentation dependencies and local coordination needs in time.

audience.title: Test the pathway before planning the submission
audience.body: MDS-G30 allows SFDA to consider certain authorisations and approvals from recognised regulatory authorities during its MDMA review. It does not remove SFDA's independent decision-making or Saudi-specific requirements.

items.title: Existing international authorisation
items.text: You hold a current approval and can provide the supporting evidence from a recognised jurisdiction.

items.title: A matched device and evidence set
items.text: The Saudi device needs to align with the authorised device in its technical characteristics and intended use.

items.title: A Saudi launch to prepare for
items.text: You need clarity on classification, local requirements and the documentation still needed before MDMA submission.

support.title: What the assessment is designed to clarify
support.subtitle: We structure the first review around the current SFDA guidance and the actual evidence available for your device. The result is a practical submission plan, not a promise of eligibility or approval.

items.title: RRA approval review
items.text: Review the reference jurisdiction, approval route, validity and evidence needed to support the reliance request.

items.title: Technical identity check
items.text: Compare the Saudi device with the authorised device, including intended use, design and manufacturing information.

items.title: Saudi requirements mapping
items.text: Identify Saudi-specific questions on classification, labelling, IFU, user interface, storage and transport.

items.title: Reliance-form preparation
items.text: Organise the required rationale and supporting information for the reliance form and MDMA application plan.

items.title: Submission-readiness roadmap
items.text: Set out the remaining workstreams, dependencies and questions to resolve with the manufacturer and local stakeholders.

eligibility.title: What the MDS-G30 assessment needs to test
eligibility.subtitle: The official guidance sets specific eligibility criteria. We use them to screen the pathway early, alongside the device's actual documentation and regulatory history.
items: Does the device hold a valid marketing authorisation or approval from a recognised regulatory authority?
Is the Saudi device technically identical to the authorised device in design, manufacturing process and intended use?
Can the application meet applicable Saudi requirements, including classification and local product requirements?

exclusions.title: Pathway limits that need early review
exclusions.subtitle: MDS-G30 identifies exclusions and circumstances that may take a device outside the reliance route or require additional information.
items: Self-registration or self-declaration routes without an independent regulatory or recognised third-party assessment.
Products granted access primarily through an equivalence-to-a-predicate route.
Custom-made devices and products with significant post-market recalls, suspensions, withdrawals or restrictions.
SaMD and AI-enabled devices may be excluded based on intended use, risk, novelty, complexity or other SFDA considerations.

items.title: Screen eligibility and exclusions
items.text: Test the available evidence against the MDS-G30 criteria and identify issues that need clarification before relying on the pathway.

items.title: Map the Saudi documentation delta
items.text: Identify Saudi-specific content and practical requirements that remain outside the reference approval.

items.title: Plan the reliance form and MDMA submission
items.text: Set out the evidence, rationale, responsibilities and next steps for a complete application plan.

faq.title: Common questions about the reliance pathway

items.question: Which international authorities are recognised in the current guidance?
items.answer: The current guidance lists Australia (TGA), Canada (Health Canada), the EU/EEA, Japan (PMDA), the UK (MHRA) and the USA (FDA). SFDA notes that this list may be updated periodically.

items.question: Does an FDA clearance automatically make a device eligible?
items.answer: No. The guidance lists FDA among the recognised authorities but excludes products granted access primarily through an equivalence-to-a-predicate route. We assess the actual authorisation route and device evidence before making a recommendation.

items.question: Does the reliance pathway guarantee an SFDA MDMA?
items.answer: No. SFDA retains full authority over the marketing authorisation decision and may request additional information or data during review.

items.question: What review time does the guidance state?
items.answer: The guidance states a standard reliance-pathway review timeline of 35–60 working days for a complete application. It also notes that review may be reduced to 35 working days where the conditions are met. This is not a guarantee for an individual submission.

focus.title: Core areas of the technical file
focus.subtitle: SFDA's medical-device marketing-authorisation requirements call for a maintained technical documentation set that demonstrates conformity with the applicable essential safety and performance principles.
items: Device description and specification, including variants and accessories in scope.
Intended purpose, intended users, qualification rationale and classification justification.
Manufacturer information, labelling, instructions for use and user-facing materials.
Applicable evidence of conformity, risk management, verification, validation and clinical or performance support.
Quality-management and manufacturing information relevant to the proposed pathway.

output.title: A prioritised readiness roadmap
output.body: We provide a structured view of the documentation available, the questions or gaps to resolve and the recommended next workstreams. The exact scope and evidence expectations must still be confirmed for the individual device and application.

faq.title: Common questions about a technical-file review

items.question: Can we start from our existing FDA, Health Canada or EU documentation?
items.answer: Existing documentation can provide a strong starting point. We assess how it maps to the proposed Saudi route and identify what needs to be adapted, confirmed or added.

items.question: Does a gap assessment guarantee an SFDA MDMA?
items.answer: No. The assessment identifies readiness questions and recommended workstreams. SFDA retains authority over the application and may require additional information.

items.question: Does the review cover labels and instructions for use?
items.answer: Yes. We include available labels, IFU and other user-facing content in the review against the applicable Saudi submission context.

items.question: When should we begin the assessment?
items.answer: Begin before a commercial launch date or submission target is fixed. Early review gives the team time to resolve evidence, document and coordination dependencies.

portfolio.eyebrow: Start with a reliable portfolio picture
portfolio.title: Information to assemble before planning
portfolio.subtitle: A productive review starts with enough detail to understand which products belong together and which questions must be handled individually.
items: Manufacturer, device family, intended purpose, models, accessories and risk-class information for each product.
Current international authorisations, available declarations and technical or quality documentation.
The proposed Saudi commercial role, source chain and launch priority for each manufacturer and device family.
Known product, manufacturing, labelling or documentation changes that could affect the next regulatory step.
Named contacts who can provide manufacturer evidence and make portfolio decisions promptly.

guidance.eyebrow: Grouping must be assessed, not assumed
guidance.title: Procedure packs and grouping need a case-by-case screen
guidance.body: SFDA's MDS-G28 guidance describes conditions for medical-device procedure packs. Whether a set of devices can be handled together depends on the exact configuration and the applicable SFDA requirements. We assess the portfolio before recommending a route.

process.title: How we structure portfolio support
process.subtitle: The aim is a clear operating view: what needs to be collected, reviewed, decided and prepared before product-level work moves forward.

items.title: Set the portfolio scope
items.text: Confirm the manufacturers, device families, launch objectives, commercial priorities and people responsible for the information.

items.question: Can every product model be included in one MDMA?
items.answer: No. Whether products or configurations can be handled together depends on the specific devices and applicable SFDA requirements. We screen each proposed group before recommending an approach.

items.question: Can you coordinate with our international manufacturers?
items.answer: Yes. We can help organise the evidence request and the regulatory workstream with the manufacturer. The manufacturer remains the source for its product and quality documentation.

items.question: Can the review include products already in the Saudi market?
items.answer: Yes. The scope can include a portfolio health check that highlights documentation, change, renewal or post-market questions requiring attention.

items.question: Does this service replace the distributor's legal or regulatory responsibilities?
items.answer: No. Responsibilities and establishment requirements depend on the specific commercial and regulatory arrangement. This service helps organise the facts and plan the work; the applicable obligations must be confirmed for the case.

privacy.intro: This notice explains how HealthUnion Global handles personal data collected through this website, including the information and documents you submit through our intake and contact forms. We design our practices to align with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Canada's PIPEDA and Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).

sections.title: Who we are
body: HealthUnion Global is a regulatory affairs consultancy supporting medical device and cosmetics manufacturers across the United States (FDA), Canada (Health Canada), Saudi Arabia (SFDA) and the wider GCC region.
We act as the data controller for the personal data collected through this website.

sections.title: Information we collect
body: We only collect what we need to respond to your request and deliver our services:
items: Details you provide through our forms: company name, contact details, product category, device classification, target markets and your message.
Regulatory documents (PDF) that you choose to upload.
Your language preference and basic technical data required to operate the site securely.
If you agree to optional measurement, limited technical and website-use data may be processed by our Google Analytics and Google Ads measurement tools.

sections.title: How we use your information
body: We use your data to respond to your enquiry and prepare a pre-diagnostic of your regulatory pathway, to provide and manage our consulting services, to communicate with you, and to meet our legal and regulatory obligations.

sections.title: Legal bases for processing
body: Depending on your location, we rely on your consent, the performance of a contract or pre-contractual steps taken at your request, and our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries.
Where the GDPR, PIPEDA or PDPL apply, we process your data in line with the rights and obligations they set out.

sections.title: Storage and security
body: Form submissions are kept in a managed database. Documents you upload are stored in encrypted object storage and are served only through authenticated requests, never through public links.
Access is limited to authorised personnel, and we apply technical and organisational measures to protect your data.

sections.title: International transfers
body: Because we operate across borders, with teams in Canada and Riyadh, your data may be processed in a country other than your own. When we transfer data internationally, we apply appropriate safeguards consistent with applicable law.

sections.title: Data retention
body: We keep your personal data only for as long as necessary to respond to your request, deliver our services and meet our legal obligations. After that, we delete or anonymise it.

sections.title: Sharing your information
body: We do not sell your data and we do not share it for advertising. We may share it with trusted service providers who help us operate this site (for example hosting and email delivery) under appropriate confidentiality commitments, and with authorities where the law requires it.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Subject to applicable law, you may request access to your data, as well as its correction, deletion, restriction or portability, and you may object to certain processing. You may also withdraw consent at any time.

sections.title: Cookies
body: We use essential cookies needed to operate the site and remember your language and cookie preferences. If optional measurement is enabled, Google Analytics and Google Ads measurement use cookies only after you give permission through Cookie Settings. You can accept or decline optional measurement at any time.

sections.title: Changes to this notice
body: We may update this notice from time to time. The "last updated" date above reflects the most recent version.

privacy.requestBody: For any question about this notice, or to exercise your rights, contact us through our contact page or by email. We respond to legitimate requests in line with applicable law.
